links.comparator_used: Dense-only and sparse-only retrieval across multiple embedding models and corpus variants
links.effect: Hybrid retrieval consistently improves recall and ranking quality; no numbers given in the abstract
links.quote: We compare dense, sparse, and hybrid retrieval across multiple embedding models and corpus variants, and show that hybrid retrieval consistently improves recall and ranking quality, with chunk length and topic interacting with ranking performance.

links.comparator_used: LLMs used without retrieval (no retrieved context)
links.effect: Providing retrieved context substantially increases multiple-choice accuracy across a diverse set of LLMs, enabling smaller open-weight models to match or outperform larger models used without retrieval
links.quote: Providing retrieved context substantially increases multiple-choice accuracy across a diverse set of LLMs, enabling smaller open-weight models to match or outperform larger models used without retrieval, with gains primarily driven by retrieval quality and careful context selection.

links.comparator_used: Dual human annotations (expert review) used to validate the rubric-based LLM judge
links.outcome: Judge-human agreement across rubric dimensions (faithfulness, completeness, clarity, factual consistency)
links.effect: Agreement strongest for faithfulness and completeness; factual consistency and clarity less reliably reproduced
links.tradeoff: Caution needed when interpreting factual consistency and clarity scores at scale
links.quote: Judge-human agreement is strongest for faithfulness and completeness, while factual consistency and clarity are less reliably reproduced, motivating caution when interpreting those dimensions at scale.
